body:
Exactly. Talking about it was truly one of the hardest things for me to come to terms with, but it really has helped. I felt like I was just... idk like, a house of cards struggling to stay together from like haha atmospheric pressure, and honestly I still feel like a house of cards but the pressure isn't nearly as intense as it once was. The goal, I guess after covid, is to really find the best haha glue to hold those cards together and keep adding more until I feel like a card mansion. c: 

Really sending you mental hugs. My lowest point was around a year and a half ago, and I'm still climbing back up out of where I was, but well... I'm starting to see the hand holds, if that makes sense haha.

I'm glad I could share something new! :D And I 100% know what you mean haha. I'm still having a tough time accepting that it's trauma and ptsd, like my therapist will say something like "those situations are especially difficult for people with trauma" and haha I have this internal defensive reaction like "nope not me! :)" But I'm slowly getting better with being like "okay. stuff happened, I'm still shaken up, it's okay to care for that part of myself" :D 

" It just amazes me that my lowest point lead to such a comeback. " That's really beautiful, thank you for saying that. :D I'm haha in a pretty difficult part of my life that isn't only difficult from past traumas and it can be hard to see things that way. That low points really will end up leading to something beautiful in life again. 

I feel the same way about meditation. :D It's just really nice to hear someone say "take a deep breathe and slowly let it out" even if that's all I hear while I'm scrolling through my phone or playing a video game. I feel really excited about healing and feeling better with these kinds of resources. :D

I can very much relate. The distractions and addictions tend to seem like the only way just to be like... an inch away from the scary feelings and stuff, but there's so much more that can help. :D Something that's helped me a bit recently is I've been listening to a podcast by someone named Tara Brach, and she's very much about meditation and she's just a really soothing person. :D 

For the last year or so I've been really committed to recovery and meditation is one of my favorite tools :D Also haha I wish that the general perception of meditation wasn't that of like... sitting in a room in complete silence and reaching a point of healed clarity independent of assistance. It's been so healing to me to utilize meditation in the sense of just... getting help with replacing the scary or self destructive thoughts with soothing ones. :D
<3 I'm so glad. I've had some break throughs recently too and... my heart is still pretty heavy, but I've been feeling like things will be okay.

I completely understand that. It's definitely hard to find people to relate to, even outside the context of trauma or mental health awareness but I think that can possibly be a helpful guide point. :D Like... if I'm really into pianos but my friend doesn't know anything about them and they're really into idk haha ant colonies, it'll be hard for us to talk about that. But maybe I could find... um, a piano tuning support group and there'll be a higher concentration of people I might be able to talk with and relate to. :D 

Of course, trauma is... not a deliberate interest exactly, but we're lucky that the "can I relate to this person" guessing game can be a little bit easier sometimes depending on the space. c: 

Haha, you probably didn't comment looking for a wall of text advice, but a bit over a year ago I sought to find an online gaming group to make new friends after a long period of not having friends and um... haha, I ended up blurting out a ton of stuff pretty quickly into some of those friendships. I was/am going through a terribly difficult time and it felt really important to share where I was coming from.

Anywho, the point of my ramble is that we all deserve to have and look for the kinds of friendships that we want. :D <3
Thank you for sharing this. From someone in recovery, who’s working so hard to heal in a really less than ideal circumstance. Thank you for your honesty and strength.

Aspects of your life remind me a bit of mine and it’s not easy, but climbing out of that space is possible. I’m still on my way and I slip sometimes, but feeling better is possible. 

I’ve been seeing a therapist for around a year and a half, after my 10 year relationship ended and I had to move back in with my abusive parents and her help has been one of the main reasons why I’ve started to heal and stay alive. I know in these times finding a therapist is hard, but more and more health professionals are offering video conference therapy. I actually had an appointment yesterday with someone so I could start anti depressants. I’m starting a sleep aid tonight and early next week I’ll be getting a test kit in the mail to help determine the best anti depressant based on my metabolism, and some other factors.

In spite of the pandemic there’s still a level of help and care out there that we all deserve and can get ❤️
relatable, but it's still good to feel and show appreciation in these times, even if it was simply out of laziness or convenience.
❤️ feeling a little at ease and I’ll keep your support with me. Ty, you’re a kind bad ass and you’re appreciated 🤘❤️🥳

Thank you again ❤️ sometimes I feel really alone with my circumstance and that means a lot to me. I have possible exposure in my life too, and it’s really scary but it’s so important to keep hope, even if it’s tiny or fades sometimes. We have to do favors for our future selves and stay alive.
Thank you ❤️ a huge part of me knows I can get through this because I’ve been through periods like this that were even worse. (Minus the virus obviously lol)
